verses.text: This is a prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, set to a song of victory.
LORD, I have heard what you are famous for. I stand in awe of your deeds, LORD. Do them again in our day. Make them known in our time. Even when you are angry, remember to show mercy.
God came from Teman. The Holy One came from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and his praise filled the earth.
His brightness was like the sunrise. Rays of light flashed from his hand, where his power was hidden.
Plague went in front of him, and disease followed close behind.
He stood and shook the earth. He looked, and the nations trembled. The ancient mountains crumbled, and the age-old hills fell down. His ways are eternal.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress. The tents of the land of Midian trembled.
LORD, were you angry with the rivers? Was your anger against the streams? Was your fury against the sea when you rode on your horses and your chariots of victory?
You took out your bow and called for many arrows. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw you and shook. Floods of water swept by. The deep sea roared and lifted its waves high.
The sun and the moon stood still in the sky at the flash of your flying arrows, at the shine of your flashing spear.
In anger you marched across the land. In fury you trampled the nations.
You came out to save your people, to save your anointed one. You crushed the leader of the land of wickedness. You stripped him from head to foot. Selah.
With his own spears you pierced the heads of his warriors when they stormed out to scatter us. They gloated as if they were about to eat up the helpless in their hiding place.
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning up the mighty waters.
I heard this, and my body trembled. My lips quivered at the sound. Decay crept into my bones, and my legs shook. Yet I will wait patiently for the day of disaster to come on the people who invade us.
Even if the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines, even if the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, even if there are no sheep in the pen and no cattle in the stalls,
yet I will celebrate in the LORD. I will be joyful in God my Savior.
The Lord GOD is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer, and he lets me walk on the high places. For the director of music. On my stringed instruments.
